problem: The sentence says the ×10 probe "multiplies the input by ten before the attenuator", which is backwards: a ×10 probe attenuates the signal, dividing it by ten, so the scope sees one tenth of the true voltage. As written it contradicts the later exam trap and would make a student divide instead of multiply.
fix: A ×10 probe attenuates the input by ten (divides it) before the attenuator, so the panel reading is one tenth of the true voltage and the panel reading must be multiplied by ten to get the actual input.

problem: "The vertical pair moves the beam up and down" can confuse a student, because the plates that deflect the beam vertically are physically mounted one above the other, not vertically.
fix: The vertical-deflection plates are the pair stacked one above the other; they push the beam up and down. The horizontal-deflection plates sit side by side and push it left and right.

problem: "Record" is used for the captured time in seconds, while "record length" in standard scope usage means the number of stored samples N. The same chapter uses "memory of depth N samples" and "record length follows from the setting", so the naming shifts under the student.
fix: Call (time/div) × divisions the record time (or acquisition time) in seconds, and reserve record length for N samples = fs × record time.

problem: "Volts per division includes the probe" reads as if the V/div setting already accounts for the probe, which is the opposite of what the calculation that follows does.
fix: Write: "The V/div setting ignores the probe. With a ×10 probe a 3.2 div peak-to-peak trace is 3.2 × 2 V/div × 10 = 64 V, not 6.4 V."
